name: fast-jwt (Node.js)
description: Performance-oriented Node JWT library used by fastify-jwt

ecosystem.comment: Node.js only: package.json declares engines.node >= 20 and the source requires node:crypto (createHmac/createSign/createVerify) plus Buffer throughout. No browser, Deno, or Bun build is published.

license.comment: package.json license field and LICENSE.md in the 6.3.0 tarball both state Apache-2.0. GitHub's licence detector reports "Other" only because the file is named LICENSE.md.

implementation.comment: All signing/verification is delegated to node:crypto in src/crypto.js (createHmac, createSign/createVerify, crypto.sign/crypto.verify). fast-jwt itself only does JSON/base64url handling, key sniffing, and ASN.1 parsing of PEM headers (asn1.js).

package.comment: Metadata verified via the npm registry API endpoint for the package.

documentation.comment: Docs site is a rendering of the README (installation, createSigner/createDecoder/createVerifier options, algorithm table, caching, JWKS pointer, benchmarks).

first-release.comment: npm registry time.created and version 0.1.0 both dated 2020-06-23.

hmac-hs.comment: src/crypto.js: hsAlgorithms = ['HS256','HS384','HS512'], implemented with createHmac; exercised in test/compliance.spec.js (HS256).

rsa-pkcs1.comment: src/crypto.js rsaAlgorithms, signed/verified with RSA_PKCS1_PADDING via node:crypto.

rsa-pss.comment: Same rsaAlgorithms list; PS* switches to RSA_PKCS1_PSS_PADDING with RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_DIGEST on sign and RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO on verify. PS384 is covered by test/compliance.spec.js.

ecdsa.comment: P-256/P-384/P-521 via node:crypto with ecdsa-sig-formatter for the JOSE↔DER conversion. ES256K is NOT a supported alg identifier: the ecCurves table in src/crypto.js maps secp256k1 (OID 1.3.132.0.10) to bits '256', so a secp256k1 key is treated as plain ES256 rather than RFC 8812 ES256K.

eddsa.comment: Registered under the RFC 8037 'EdDSA' alg identifier only (no curve-specific 'Ed25519' alg id). src/crypto.js accepts both OID 1.3.101.112 (Ed25519) and 1.3.101.113 (Ed448) and returns 'EdDSA'; the curve is taken from the key. Ed25519 is exercised in test/compliance.spec.js.

jwe-key-management.comment: fast-jwt implements JWS compact tokens only; there is no JWE code path in src/.

jwe-content-encryption.comment: No JWE support, so no content-encryption algorithms.

deprecated-algorithms-available.comment: 'none' is a first-class supported algorithm: createSigner({ algorithm: 'none' }) emits unsecured tokens (and refuses a key), and a verifier configured with algorithms: ['none'] and a null key accepts them. secp256k1 keys are accepted but mapped onto the ES256 identifier instead of RFC 8812 ES256K, i.e. the curve is usable without its own restricted alg id.

algorithm-extensibility.comment: The supported set is a fixed Set in src/signer.js (HS/ES/RS/PS/EdDSA + none) and a fixed union type in src/index.d.ts; there is no registration hook for a custom alg.

rejects-alg-none.comment: On the default path in src/verifier.js the allowed-algorithm list is derived from the supplied key (detectPublicKeyAlgorithms), which never yields 'none'; an unsecured token then fails with FAST_JWT_INVALID_ALGORITHM. With no key the list stays empty and 'none' is still rejected. Accepting it requires the explicit opt-in createVerifier({ key: null, algorithms: ['none'] }). Note the README's claim that "by default, all algorithms are accepted" is looser than the code.

algorithm-pinning.comment: createVerifier infers the accepted algorithms from the key material (RSA PEM → RS*/PS*, EC PEM → ES<bits>, OKP → EdDSA, anything without a PEM header → HS*), and only narrows that set if the caller passes `algorithms`. The inference is a textual PEM sniff rather than a structural key type, which is exactly the mechanism behind the CVE-2023-48223 / CVE-2026-34950 / GHSA-ww5h-9m49-7xx4 confusion lineage; every advisory recommends passing an explicit `algorithms` allow-list.

algorithm-confusion-resistance.comment: Keys are raw strings/Buffers for every algorithm; RSA-key-as-HMAC-secret is prevented only by string sniffing (locatePem + publicKeyPemMatcher, plus a new check refusing serialized asymmetric JWK/JWKS JSON as an HMAC secret). That heuristic has been bypassed three times — CVE-2023-48223 (fixed 3.3.2), CVE-2026-34950 (whitespace prefix), and GHSA-ww5h-9m49-7xx4 (non-whitespace prefix, fixed 2026-07-28 in 6.3.0). 6.3.0 hardens it into a single locatePem helper, but the guideline's level 2 ("raw bytes/strings accepted, documentation warns against misuse") is the honest rating given the track record; passing `algorithms` explicitly raises the practical level to 3.

unverified-decode-separated.comment: createDecoder() is a separate top-level export in src/decoder.js that never touches a key or a signature; verification lives only in createVerifier(). The decoder name is not alarming ("decode" rather than "unsafeDecode"), but the two APIs are genuinely distinct and the verifier has no "skip verification" flag.

default-claim-validation.comment: createVerifier registers nbf and exp validators unless ignoreNotBefore/ignoreExpiration are set. iat is only checked when maxAge is given; aud/iss/sub/jti/nonce only when the corresponding allowed* option is passed; typ only with checkTyp; requiredClaims defaults to none, so a token with no exp at all still verifies.

audience-issuer-required.comment: allowedAud and allowedIss are optional; the README states "by default, all values are accepted". Callers can approximate fail-closed behaviour with requiredClaims: ['aud','iss'] plus the allowed* options, but nothing forces it.

clock-skew-configurable.comment: clockTolerance (milliseconds) defaults to 0, and clockTimestamp can pin the reference time. Since GHSA-687g-22h4-j4w4 ("infinite clock tolerance bypasses exp and nbf") the option is validated as a finite, non-negative number.

constant-time-comparison.comment: src/crypto.js verifySignature compares HMAC tags with node:crypto timingSafeEqual, returning false when the lengths differ. Asymmetric algorithms use node:crypto verify directly.

minimum-key-size-enforced.comment: No RSA modulus-size check anywhere in src/; a 1024-bit RSA key verifies. HMAC secrets are only checked for being non-empty (added after GHSA-gmvf-9v4p-v8jc / CVE-2026-44351), not for the RFC 7518 §3.2 requirement of at least hash-output length.

crit-header-handling.comment: validateCrit in src/verifier.js enforces RFC 7515 §4.1.11: crit must be a non-empty string array, must not name registered headers, must not contain duplicates, every entry must appear in the header, and every entry must be listed in the caller's allowedCritHeaders — otherwise FAST_JWT_INVALID_CRIT_HEADER. This behaviour was added in response to GHSA-hm7r-c7qw-ghp6 / CVE-2026-35042 (April 2026); earlier versions ignored crit.

nested-depth-limits.comment: Not applicable: fast-jwt handles single-level compact JWS only — no JWE, no nested tokens, no PBES2 iteration counts, so there is nothing to depth-limit. The related DoS surface it does address is ReDoS in user-supplied allowed* RegExps (safe-regex2 warning, after GHSA-cjw9-ghj4-fwxf).

cve-history.comment: Ten repository advisories as of 2026-07-30, most of them in 2026. Highlights: GHSA-c2ff-88x2-x9pg / CVE-2023-48223 (algorithm confusion, fixed 3.3.2); GHSA-gm45-q3v2-6cf8 / CVE-2025-30144 (iss validation); GHSA-mvf2-f6gm-w987 / CVE-2026-34950 (incomplete fix, whitespace-prefixed RSA key); GHSA-rp9m-7r4c-75qg / CVE-2026-35039 (cache key collisions); GHSA-hm7r-c7qw-ghp6 / CVE-2026-35042 (crit ignored); GHSA-cjw9-ghj4-fwxf and GHSA-3j8v-cgw4-2g6q (ReDoS / stateful RegExp); GHSA-gmvf-9v4p-v8jc / CVE-2026-44351 (empty HMAC secret via async key resolver); and three published 2026-07-28: GHSA-ww5h-9m49-7xx4 (critical, non-whitespace key prefix re-enables confusion, affects 6.2.0–6.2.4), GHSA-g3jj-5cmm-3hxx (raw public JWK JSON accepted as HMAC secret) and GHSA-5hjw-83fp-phq9 (claim validators bypassed for array payloads). All are patched in 6.3.0; no unpatched advisory was found.

security-policy.comment: Borderline: there is no SECURITY.md (GitHub shows "This project has not set up a SECURITY.md file yet"), but GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled — the security tab offers "Report a vulnerability" and the maintainers routinely publish repository advisories with fixes. Counted as a documented private disclosure channel.

independent-security-review.comment: Searched for a published third-party audit and found none; the security record consists of coordinated researcher disclosures handled through GitHub advisories. NearForm has credited informal review from JOSE experts in blog posts, which does not meet the bar for a published audit.

jws.comment: createSigner and createVerifier cover both directions for compact JWS.

jwe.comment: No JWE implementation; the library is JWT/JWS only.

jwk-parsing.comment: Keys must be PEM strings/Buffers or raw HMAC secrets. Since GHSA-g3jj-5cmm-3hxx, serialized JWK/JWKS JSON is explicitly rejected rather than parsed. Converting JWK to PEM is left to the caller (or to get-jwks).

jwks-remote-fetch.comment: The docs state "JWKS is supported via get-jwks" — a separate NearForm package used as the verifier's async key function. fast-jwt itself performs no HTTP.

jwks-caching-rotation.comment: Delegated to the companion get-jwks package. fast-jwt's own LRU cache caches verification results (tokens), not key sets.

kid-selection.comment: The library never selects a key by kid. It passes the decoded token ({ header, payload, signature }) to the caller's async key function, so kid-based lookup is possible but entirely the caller's (or get-jwks') job. Signing can set the kid header.

jwk-thumbprint.comment: No RFC 7638 thumbprint computation in src/.

nested-jwt.comment: Requires JWE, which is not implemented.

json-serialization.comment: src/decoder.js splits on the two dots of the compact form; flattened/general JSON serialization and multiple signatures are not supported.

detached-payload.comment: The decoder requires a non-empty payload segment; no RFC 7515 Appendix F support.

unencoded-payload.comment: No RFC 7797 b64:false handling; the decoder rejects any segment outside the base64url alphabet.

key-generation.comment: No key-generation API; the README documents ssh-keygen/openssl commands for producing test keys.

x509-header-support.comment: x5c/x5t/x5t#S256/x5u appear only in the JwtHeader TypeScript type and in the crit deny-list; no X.509 header parameter is read, resolved, or validated during verification. A PEM X.509 certificate can be passed as the key value (it is converted to SPKI via createPublicKey), but that is key input, not header support.

key-input-formats.comment: src/crypto.js recognises PEM PKCS#1 (BEGIN RSA ...), SEC1 (BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY), PKCS#8 (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY / ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY, with a passphrase object), SPKI (BEGIN PUBLIC KEY) and PEM X.509 certificates; anything with no PEM header is treated as a raw HMAC secret. Binary DER, JWK and JWKS are not accepted (JWK/JWKS JSON is now actively refused).

external-signer-support.comment: The key option may be a function, but it must resolve to a string/Buffer key the library then signs with itself — there is no pluggable signer interface, so KMS/HSM signing is not possible.

framework-integrations.comment: @fastify/jwt 10.2.1 depends on fast-jwt ^6.2.4 — the official Fastify JWT plugin is a first-party wrapper around this library. No Express/NestJS/Hono adapter is published by the maintainers.

async-api.comment: Signer/verifier are synchronous when the key is a string or Buffer, and switch to callback-or-promise style when the key option is a function (e.g. a JWKS resolver). The typings overload createSigner/createVerifier accordingly.

typed-claims.comment: src/index.d.ts types the verifier's result as `any` and the decoded payload as `any`; the generic parameter on createSigner/createVerifier constrains the input payload/token type only. Claims are plain JSON objects with no schema validation beyond the built-in type checks on registered claims.

crypto-backend.comment: Everything runs through node:crypto, which in mainline Node.js is backed by OpenSSL. fast-jwt neither bundles nor selects a crypto provider itself.

pure-language-implementation.comment: The five direct dependencies (asn1.js, mnemonist, @lukeed/ms, safe-regex2, ecdsa-sig-formatter) are all pure JavaScript; there is no native addon or FFI in the install. The cryptography itself is native, but inside Node's own runtime rather than a package dependency.

runs-in-browser-wasm.comment: Hard dependency on node:crypto and Buffer, CommonJS entry point, engines.node >= 20, and no browser field or bundled build. Only usable in a browser through a Node-polyfilling bundler, which is not a supported configuration.

edge-runtime-compatible.comment: Needs node:crypto createSign/createVerify/createHmac and PEM key objects; the docs make no claim about Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, or Deno Deploy, and no edge target is tested in CI. Might partially work under Workers' nodejs_compat, but that is unverified — treated as not supported.

fips-capable-backend.comment: Indirect: because all primitives come from node:crypto, running on a Node.js build linked against a FIPS-validated OpenSSL provider (node --enable-fips) puts the operations inside that module. The validation belongs to the OpenSSL module, not to fast-jwt, which offers no FIPS switch of its own and would fail on any algorithm the FIPS provider blocks (e.g. Ed25519 in some configurations).

dependency-count.comment: Direct runtime dependencies of 6.3.0: asn1.js, mnemonist, @lukeed/ms, safe-regex2, ecdsa-sig-formatter (checked 2026-07-30).

package-size.comment: dist.unpackedSize for 6.3.0 (11 files: README, LICENSE, package.json and eight src files).

downloads.comment: npm downloads for the week 2026-07-23 to 2026-07-29. Node ecosystem window: weekly. A large share arrives through @fastify/jwt.

last-release.comment: 6.3.0, the security release fixing the three advisories published the same day.

maintenance-status.comment: Six releases in the last four months, last push 2026-07-29, and advisories are patched on the day they are published. Maintained by NearForm; no deprecation notice.

bus-factor.comment: Company-backed: the repository lives in the NearForm org, npm maintainers are mostly NearForm staff, releases are automated (optic-release-automation), and recent commits come from several different humans plus dependabot rather than a single author.

maturity.comment: 6.x with a stable, documented API, five years of history and heavy production use via @fastify/jwt. Held short of "mature" deliberately: eight of ten advisories — including three critical auth-bypass classes — were published in 2026, so the track record of getting the security-critical defaults right is still being established, even though the response time is good.

rfc-conformance-testing.comment: test/compliance.spec.js builds its HS256/RS256/PS384/ES512/EdDSA cases on keys lifted from RFC 7520 and RFC 8037, and test/compatibility.spec.js cross-checks against jsonwebtoken and jose. The published RFC signature vectors themselves are not replayed, so the suite is mostly self-generated round-trip testing on standard keys.

documentation-quality.comment: Complete option-by-option reference for createSigner/createDecoder/createVerifier with runnable sync, callback and promise examples, an algorithm table, error-code handling and a detailed caching section including its security caveat. Short of 5: no dedicated security-considerations section (the algorithm-pinning advice that the advisories all give is absent), and JWKS is a one-line pointer to get-jwks.
